name: Aystat Detect Hidden
author: stonemanhero

sections.description:
Aystat Detect Hidden is an advanced security auditing and threat remediation plugin designed to expose stealth malware, backdoor administrators, rogue privilege escalations, concealed posts, hidden doorway pages, clandestine plugins, hidden themes, and stealth WP-Cron persistence tasks.

The Problem: Hook-Based Cloaking & Database Tampering

Modern WordPress malware rarely modifies core files directly. Instead, sophisticated attackers and backdoors insert malicious users, privilege grants, or content into your database and hook into WordPress filter APIs to keep them invisible:

  • Hidden Users, Rogue Capabilities & Orphaned Usermeta
    Malware adds a rogue administrator account to the wp_users database table, then registers a hook on pre_user_query to filter its own ID out of all standard WordPress queries. Attackers also inject direct high-privilege capability grants (manage_options, edit_users, install_plugins, unfiltered_html) onto low-privilege accounts (such as a subscriber or customer), or leave orphaned wp_capabilities rows in wp_usermeta for deleted user IDs ready for instant privilege re-hydration.

  • Concealed Posts & Doorway Pages
    Attackers insert SEO spam, phishing forms, or doorway pages into wp_posts, then manipulate pre_get_posts or posts_where so the posts never appear in the WordPress Admin post list.

  • Concealed Plugins
    Rogue plugins or backdoors hook into the all_plugins filter to hide themselves from the /wp-admin/plugins.php interface while continuing to execute on every HTTP request.

  • Concealed & Unmanaged Themes
    Attackers plant backdoor themes or rogue PHP shells inside wp-content/themes/ and filter wp_prepare_themes_for_js or allowed_themes to hide them from Appearance > Themes.

The Solution: Differential Auditing & Hook Inspection

Aystat Detect Hidden bypasses hooked filters through deep differential comparison and multi-layered defense-in-depth:

  1. User & Privilege Differential Audit
    Fetches visible users via standard get_users() queries and compares them against raw database rows queried directly from {$wpdb->users} and {$wpdb->usermeta}. Flags concealed user accounts, non-administrator accounts holding direct high-privilege capability grants (ROGUE CAPS), and orphaned privileged wp_usermeta records (ORPHANED META) missing from wp_users.

  2. Post & Page Differential Audit
    Executes WP_Query with active filters and compares returned IDs against raw database records from {$wpdb->posts}. Any post or page omitted from the API query is flagged.

  3. Plugin & Component Audit
    Physically inspects the plugins directory via DirectoryIterator (supporting subdirectories, single-file plugins, and unmanaged standalone PHP scripts) and compares physical files against filtered all_plugins hook output.

  4. MU-Plugin & Core Drop-in Inspection
    Enumerates all active Must-Use plugins and core architectural drop-ins in the content directory, highlighting high-privilege drop-ins (db.php, object-cache.php) with elevated security advisories.

  5. Themes Differential Audit
    Physically scans get_theme_root() (wp-content/themes/) via DirectoryIterator and compares on-disk theme directories and standalone .php files against wp_prepare_themes_for_js() and allowed_themes filter outputs.

  6. WP-Cron Jobs Differential Audit
    Compares filtered _get_cron_array() schedules against the raw serialized cron option row in {$wpdb->options} to uncover stealth persistence tasks cloaked via option_cron or pre_option_cron filters, inspecting attached callbacks via PHP Reflection.

  7. Enhanced Hook & Query Inspector with Inline Code Preview
    Leverages PHP Reflection to analyze callbacks on sensitive filters (query, pre_user_query, get_user_metadata, all_plugins, wp_prepare_themes_for_js, allowed_themes, posts_where, option_cron, pre_option_cron), revealing exact file paths, declaration line numbers, anonymous closures, and a 1-click View Code read-only modal with ±5 lines of surrounding context.

Advanced Edition Upgrades

Need 1-click threat remediation, client reporting, and autonomous background monitoring? Aystat Detect Hidden Advanced adds:

  • 1-Click Safe Remediation
    Instantly delete rogue users, purge orphaned privileged usermeta, trash spam posts, delete concealed themes (with active-theme safety guards), unschedule concealed WP-Cron persistence tasks, and delete unauthorized backdoor plugin files with strict path traversal safeguards.

  • PDF / JSON Exportable Security Audit Reports
    Generate client-ready PDF/Print Security Audit Certificates and machine-readable JSON audit snapshots to prove to clients that their database and hooks were audited for stealth malware.

  • WP-CLI Automation (wp aystat audit --format=json)
    Run differential security audits across agency multi-site fleets, SSH scripts, and CI/CD pipelines from the command line.

  • False-Positive Whitelisting
    Ignore approved exceptions (custom tools, custom capabilities, themes, or intentional drop-ins) with a single click, keeping your audit reports clean.

  • Autonomous 24/7 Background Scans
    Scheduled WP-Cron runner with configurable scan frequencies (Hourly, 2h, 3h, 6h, 12h, Daily, Weekly).

  • Smart State-Diff Email Alerts
    Zero email fatigue — alerts dispatched only when new threats appear or threat status changes.

  • Priority Security Support
    Direct developer assistance and priority updates.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the aystat-detect-hidden folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install directly through the WordPress plugin installer.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Tools > Detect Hidden in your WordPress admin menu.
  4. Click Run Security Audit to execute a full differential analysis.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin affect frontend site speed?

No. Audits execute only when an administrator triggers a scan in the admin dashboard. Zero queries or hooks are added to front-end visitor traffic.

What makes this scanner different from other security plugins?

Standard security plugins ask WordPress APIs for lists of users, plugins, and themes. If stealth malware has hooked pre_user_query, all_plugins, or wp_prepare_themes_for_js, standard plugins are blinded by the same hooks. Aystat Detect Hidden queries the database tables and filesystem directly to uncover hidden discrepancies.

What is the difference between Free and Advanced?

The Free version on WordPress.org provides 100% complete differential auditing across users, privilege grants, orphaned usermeta, posts, plugins, drop-ins, themes, WP-Cron jobs, and hook inspection (including inline source code preview). The separate Advanced edition adds 1-click automated threat deletion (users, orphaned usermeta, posts, plugin files, themes, cron jobs), false-positive whitelisting, exportable PDF & JSON client security audit reports, WP-CLI automation (wp aystat audit --format=json), and 24/7 background WP-Cron scans with smart email alerts.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Added Hidden & Unmanaged Themes Differential Scanner (Themes metric card and tab), comparing physical wp-content/themes/ directories and loose .php files against wp_prepare_themes_for_js() and allowed_themes outputs.
  • Upgraded Users Scanner to detect Rogue Administrator Capabilities (ROGUE CAPS, direct high-privilege capability grants on non-administrator accounts) and Orphaned Privileged Usermeta (ORPHANED META in wp_usermeta with no matching wp_users record).
  • Added Hidden WP-Cron Jobs Differential Scanner (cron option differential) in a dedicated Cron Jobs tab, comparing _get_cron_array() against raw {$wpdb->options} records and inspecting attached callbacks via PHP Reflection.
  • Added Inline Source Code Preview Modal (“View Code”) to the Hook Inspector, allowing administrators to inspect the exact PHP callback lines (with ±5 lines of surrounding context) in read-only mode.
  • Added wp_prepare_themes_for_js, allowed_themes, get_user_metadata, pre_option_cron, and option_cron monitoring to the Hook & Query Interception Inspector.
  • Moved Hook & Query Interception Inspector to a dedicated dashboard tab located between Cron Jobs and Advanced Edition.
  • Hook and query driver inspections are now strictly informational diagnostics and no longer count toward active threats or auditing status.
  • Redesigned 6-card metric dashboard with full-height icon strips, dynamic threat icon highlighting, WordPress site timezone timestamp formatting, and threat-only circular tab count badges.
  • Updated User Guide, contextual Help tabs, and documentation.

1.0.4

  • Added Enhanced Hook & Query Interception Inspector using PHP Reflection: extracts exact file paths, line numbers, closure detection, and provenance classification.
  • Added actionable Threats Found card navigation with automatic tab switching and smooth scrolling to flagged items.
  • Added False-Positive Whitelist (Ignore/Unignore) feature to approve legitimate exceptions.
  • Added Clear Scan Snapshot action to reset cached scan states safely.
  • Updated file and directory path resolution to use core WordPress path functions.
  • Removed all locked/premium-gated code to ensure 100% free, unrestricted functionality in the WordPress.org edition.

1.0.3

  • Added defense-in-depth low-level SQL query filter isolation to defeat in-memory query rewrites.
  • Added critical alert detection for active hooks on the WordPress query filter.
  • Added unmanaged standalone PHP script and headerless plugin directory detection.
  • Added elevated security warning badge and advisories for db.php and object-cache.php drop-ins.
  • Added runtime database driver class integrity checks.

1.0.2

  • Added perceptible live scanning states and execution time reporting.
  • Added persistent audit state on page reload.
  • Scalability optimizations for databases with 30,000+ users and high post counts.

1.0.1

  • Enhanced button flex layout and Dashicons alignment to prevent line-wrapping.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release with differential user, post, and plugin auditing.
